def priority(item: float, bins: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    remaining = bins - item
    # Set priority to 0 for bins that cannot fit the item
    priority_scores = np.where(remaining < 0, 0, remaining)
    # Invert the priority so that smaller remaining capacity (closer to fitting) has higher priority
    # Use a small epsilon to avoid division by zero
    epsilon = 1e-10
    priority_scores = 1 / (priority_scores + epsilon)
    # Ensure bins that can't fit the item have lowest priority
    priority_scores = np.where(remaining < 0, 0, priority_scores)
    return priority_scores

    remaining = bins - item

    priorities = np.zeros_like(bins)
    # Target optimal remaining capacity is half of the bin capacity

    # Compute deviation from target remaining capacity

    # Invert deviation so smaller deviation means higher priority

def priority(item: float, bins: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Returns priority with which we want to add item to each bin.
    Args:
        item: Size of item to be added to the bin.
        bins: Array of capacities for each bin.
    Return:
        Array of same size as bins with priority score of each bin.
    """
    remaining = bins - item
    valid = remaining >= 0
    priorities = np.full_like(bins, -1e10)
    
    # Post-addition remaining capacity
    post_add_remaining = remaining
    # Normalize by bin size to avoid bias from bin size differences
    normalized_remaining = post_add_remaining / (bins + 1e-10)
    
    # Use log of (1 + normalized_remaining) to penalize both very small and very large residuals
    # This encourages moderate, balanced residual sizes
    log_penalty = np.log(1 + normalized_remaining)
    
    # Higher priority for bins with more balanced residuals (moderate log value)
    # Invert to turn lower penalty into higher priority
    priorities[valid] = 1 / (log_penalty[valid] + 1e-10)
    return priorities

def priority(item: float, bins: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    remaining = bins - item
    # Set priority to 0 for bins that cannot fit the item
    valid_bins = remaining >= 0
    priority_scores = np.zeros_like(bins)
    # For bins that can fit the item, compute priority as the ratio of item size to remaining capacity
    # This rewards bins where the item takes up a larger fraction of the available space
    with np.errstate(divide='ignore', invalid='ignore'):
        ratio = item / (remaining + 1e-10)
        priority_scores[valid_bins] = ratio
    return priority_scores

def priority(item: float, bins: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    remaining = bins - item
    valid = remaining >= 0
    priorities = np.full_like(bins, -1e10)
    
    target_fraction = 0.3
    target_remaining = bins * target_fraction
    deviation = np.abs(remaining - target_remaining)
    
    epsilon = 1e-10
    priorities[valid] = 1 / (deviation[valid] + epsilon)
    return priorities
